SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE AND PLANS
File number: 23025-T1

17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 2652 West Chicago Avenue, Chicago, IL

Proposed Zoning: B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District

Lot Area: 15,625 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
four-story mixed-use building that will contain 1,680 sq. ft. of retail space
and four (4) residential dwelling units at grade and thirty-six (36) residential
dwelling units above. The proposed building will measure 48 feet and 314
inches in height. The subject property is a Transit Served Location and will
be supported by twenty-three (23) off-street parking spaces and forty-eight
(48) bicycle parking spaces. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional
Administrative Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to Sees. 17-13-
1003-EE and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the residential off-street parking ratio from
50% (20 parking spaces) to 57.5% (23 parking spaces), reduce the rear
setback for floors containing residential units from 30 ft. to zero, and is
seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Chicago Zoning code, for the

attached plans.

(A) | The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 43,766 square feet (2.081 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 390,625 square feet per D.U.
(40 dwelling units proposed)

(C) The amount of off-street parking: 23 parking spaces
*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to the Chicago CTA Bus Route. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the off-street parking ratio from 50% (20 parking
spaces) to 57.5% (23 parking spaces).

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback: zero

b. Side Setbacks:
West Side: zero
East Side: Zero
c. Rear Setback: zero

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential units from 30 feet to zero.

(E) Building Height: 48 feet and 3% inches

Final for Publication

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1, The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it abuts the Chicago CTA Bus Route at the West Chicago Avenue and North
Washtenaw Avenue bus stop. The proposed mixed-use building containing retail space and
four (4) dwelling units at grade and thirty-six (36) residential units above will be supported
by twenty-three (23) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the residential off-street parking ratio from 50% (20
parking spaces) to 57.5% (23 parking spaces).

2, The Applicant’s building design complies with the requirements of Sec. 17-4-0504 because
the residential entrance and the retail portion of the proposed building fronts along West
Chicago Avenue. The building’s first floor is designed with widows facing the sidewalk
along West Chicago Avenue and North Washtenaw Avenue and the building’s proposed

front setback is zero.

3, The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Chicago CTA Bus Route. The Applicant believes the development will
improve the subject area for residents and other commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain a retail unit, four (4) residential dwelling
units, and parking garage at on the first floor. The proposed building will contain thirty-six
(36) residential dwelling units on floors two through four and a roof top deck. The building
will be supported by twenty-three (23) off-street garage parking spaces and forty-eight (48)
onsite bicycle parking spaces. The Applicant is seeking administrative approval to permit
the off-street parking ratio of 57.5% for the residential units pursuant to the TOD
Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood, More specifically, the project will replace a vacant
commercial building with a surface parking lot with a new mixed-use building offering
new retail space along West Chicago Avenue. The proposed. residential units will provide
additional residential housing inventory to meet market demand. Based on the subject
property’s proximity to mass transit, the Applicant believes the project provides transit
options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules
promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an area in need.

Final for Publication
